title: Barcode recognition does not proofread a chemically captured wrong donor by itself
statement: For exponential correct/wrong precursor capture alpha_C,alpha_W, commitment c_C,c_W and competent reversal r_C,r_W, let A=alpha_C*c_C/(c_C+r_C), B=alpha_W*c_W/(c_W+r_W). With no other permanent exit, P_C=A/(A+B) and mean completion time T=[1+alpha_C/(c_C+r_C)+alpha_W/(c_W+r_W)]/(A+B). If correct/wrong commitment and reversal kinetics match, B/A=alpha_W/alpha_C; a DNA label or departure alone adds no discrimination.

requires: Finite nonnegative rates with alpha_C>0,c_C>0,c_W+r_W>0, hence A>0 for the B/A ratio; initial competent root and identical competent state after reversal.
No other permanent exit, aging, donor depletion or history change; real rate coupling to recognition must be separately supplied.

assumptions: Wrong chemical capture before recognition is permitted by the model; mismatch does not prove chemical exclusion.
The shared-kinetics equality is not a no-proofreading theorem for systems that actually couple recognition to chemical reversal/commitment.

body: Each capture is followed by a competing irreversible commitment or chemical reversal back to the same competent uncaptured root. First-step success equations weight each capture by its commitment probability; reversing branches renew. Dwell-time equations retain time in both precursors and yield the displayed numerator. Chemical disassembly is the relevant r, not merely loss of a DNA duplex after covalent precursor formation. The actual source function has only capture, commitment and reversal arguments; its common-off loop changes shared chemical reversal and preserves capture-ratio odds. Any DNA-state coupling must demonstrably change actual chemical rates or prevent access. A self-silencing end product does not itself supply selective precursor capture. The source256-donor concentration/reversal numbers extrapolate an isolated component proxy under equal accessibility, fixed kinetics and a supplied correct-capture rate; scaffold exclusion/caging can invalidate those premises. Heterocyclic end products, donor-DNA ejection and site-specific identity remain separate physical interfaces.
